answer.diagnosis: Many first-layer units carry very large weights (|60-99|, far above their other weights) on a small 3x3 patch at image rows 1-3, columns 1-3 in the top-left corner. Blob size cannot explain this: the blob sits near the centre, and the corner should be background. The sign of the patch weights lines up with each unit's role. Units 1, 7, 11, 12, 14, 16 and 19 have strong positive patch weights. Most of them are 'blob-interior' detectors (positive centre disc). Units 3, 5, 8, 10, 17, 20, 23, 25, 30 and 31 have strong negative patch weights. Most of them are ring/background detectors. All of these feed layer 2 and drive the logit. So a bright mark in the top-left corner pushes the logit, which points to a spurious corner marker that was correlated with the label in training. The genuine size features (centre discs and annular rings) live in the same units and are left untouched. The edit removes the corner-patch weights from every first-layer unit, so the corner can no longer influence the output.

edits.reason: remove spurious top-left corner marker detector
